nodeData.topic: Day 01 · The Spiritual Science Behind Brahma-muhurta
nodeData.note: SB 10.70.4 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The opening class of the series, only partly captured in the recording: Krishna's own early rising in Dvaraka, the instruction to chant and remember on waking, the Gurvastaka's promise for those who sing it at brahma-muhurta, and Srila Prabhupada's personal example and vigilance about the morning program. It closes with a question on why long practice does not always show a change of heart. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Devotees are asked to join a new Zoom link where Maharaj's slides (a PDF) are shown. Much of this recording is silent or untranscribed, so only parts of the class survive.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:26 (auto-transcript): “in the Maharaj's PDF, in Maharaj's class and you can see the PDF when Maharaj is here. Please join the new Zoom link, I have shared you the Zoom link in your groups. Please join the new Zoom link.”
A slide reads the verse describing Krishna's own routine as a householder in Dvaraka: rising in brahma-muhurta and meditating on the Absolute Truth.

Maharaj points back to chapter 70 and asks the class what Krishna does at that hour — the Lord's own daily routine is the model for the devotee's morning.

🎙 Maharaj at 69:55 (auto-transcript): “boba is very nature ever dispels of contamination on pure and blissful existence 1070 what does he do Chant Hare Krishna or at least Krishna Krishna Krishna in this way one should”

A passage on the morning is read: on waking one should chant Hare Krishna, or at least Krishna's name, remember him and recite prayers; this makes the start of the day auspicious and above the influence of the modes.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:22 (auto-transcript): “Chant Hare Krishna or at least Krishna Krishna Krishna in this way one should”

children.topic: Mind your last thoughts before sleep
children.note:
Maharaj adds that the morning begins the night before: one should be careful about what one thinks of before going to sleep.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:43 (auto-transcript): “Be mindful of what one thinks about before we escape. Yes. Yes, the”

The closing verse of Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's prayer to the spiritual master is read: one who sings these eight verses carefully and loudly at brahma-muhurta attains direct service to Krishna, the Lord of Vrindavan, at the end of life.

🎙 Maharaj at 90:44 (auto-transcript): “attention loudly recites this beautiful prayer of eight verses to the spiritual master during the Brahmurta obtains direct service to the Lord the Lord of Vrindavan at the end of his life. One who, with great care and attention, loudly recites this beautiful prayer of eight…”

Slides quote Srila Prabhupada saying he himself follows this process every morning — going to the temple, seeing the deity and offering obeisances.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:45 (auto-transcript): “I also follow this process. Every morning I go to the temple and see the deity and offer obeisances.”

From a letter: Prabhupada expects each disciple to follow the same — rising early, bathing and attending mangala-arati.

🎙 Maharaj at 95:47 (auto-transcript): “So I expect each and every one of my disciples should also follow what I have given in this connection. Rising early, taking bath, attending Magalarti. Letter to Relashan. We said it didn't give us an experimental thing, Prabhupada gave us his full condition.”

Maharaj stresses that Prabhupada did not give us something experimental; he gave the full, tested standard.

🎙 Maharaj at 95:59 (auto-transcript): “We said it didn't give us an experimental thing, Prabhupada gave us his full condition.”

A memory is read from a camp in the cold season: the brahmacaris stayed in their sleeping bags and came late to mangala-arati, so Prabhupada, though unwell, rose at 4 a.m., sat under the pump, took an ice-cold bath and came to the program — and it deeply moved them all.

🎙 Maharaj at 97:38 (auto-transcript): “30 and I walked all the way from our camp to the Ganges to take an early morning bath. But those of us staying in the Brahmachari tent were not so strong and generally when it was the time to get up at 4 o'clock it was so cold out and we preferred to remain in our sleeping…”

Commenting on the story, the class notes how amazing it was that Prabhupada pushed them to follow even in such conditions — and for those who tried, the water pumped from the ground early in the morning was not so cold; it was the air that was cold.

🎙 Maharaj at 100:41 (auto-transcript): “So Prabhupada, amazing, trying to tell us to follow even in these conditions. But it was amazing because for those who tried, it's actually that when the water is pumped from the ground early morning, it's actually not so cold. The water from the ground is not cold, but the…”

Another account is read: some devotees went on an early parikrama to avoid the day's heat and came back after Prabhupada's lecture had begun. He was displeased — hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam in the morning program is more important, so no more early parikramas.

🎙 Maharaj at 101:13 (auto-transcript): “Aikpaya Chalpatari went out on Parikrama very early to avoid the heat of the day but”

Prabhupada watched who attended. He called the temple president to ask why some devotees were regularly absent: mangala-arati is very important, everyone must come, and punctuality matters too.

🎙 Maharaj at 102:46 (auto-transcript): “Prabhupada was vigilant. Sorry. Prabhupada was vigilant about the devotees' attendance and the morning program. Calling for the technical president, he asked why some devotees were regularly absent. Mangalarthi, he said, was very important and everyone must attend.…”

A slide describes brahma-muhurta as a treasure: longed for, carefully protected, it creates eagerness.

🎙 Maharaj at 105:04 (auto-transcript): “A treasure longed for internal attraction, carefully protected, creates eagerness.”

If this hour is valued and kept in this way, the class hears, we should become pure devotees very soon.

🎙 Maharaj at 106:55 (auto-transcript): “Then we should become pure devotees very soon.”

One question from a participant and a comment from another devotee; Maharaj's own answer is not captured in the recording.

🎙 Maharaj at 115:01 (auto-transcript): “Because most of the importance is given and all the most important limbs of bhakti is covered in those 4-5 hours. but we have also seen that many devotees living in the movement for 20-25 years following Rambamurad Mahalati very nicely, chanting Guru Ashtaka prayers consisted…”

children.topic: Q1 · Years of sadhana, no change?
children.note:
Many devotees have followed the full morning program for 20–25 years — mangala-arati, Gurvastaka, guru-puja, Bhagavatam class — yet the change of heart is not visible, and some newcomers seem softer and more humane. How should we understand this?

🎙 Maharaj at 115:07 (auto-transcript): “but we have also seen that many devotees living in the movement for 20-25 years following Rambamurad Mahalati very nicely, chanting Guru Ashtaka prayers consisted in Guru Puja, Bhagavatam class but we see that change in heart is not visible like devotees who are moving into…”

A devotee comments that sincerity is the one thing required, but people arrive from very different places: some carry realisation from previous lives and chant 16 rounds from the first day; others come from a sinful background and attend Sunday programs for 15 years before asking who Krishna is.

🎙 Maharaj at 120:58 (auto-transcript): “I'm just wanting to comment that in my experience it's like many different kinds of people coming to the movement and sincerity, Prabhupada says, is definitely the only thing required. with some people we have to understand that they have already been involved with spiritual…”

children.topic: Progress measured from where one began
children.note:
So we should be merciful: someone may seem not to have progressed, yet has progressed relative to where they started, and hearing will increase their sincerity and determination.

🎙 Maharaj at 122:27 (auto-transcript): “I was just a little afraid of, it's true, we seem to observe sometimes that people have not progressed, but they have progressed according to where they were before. At least some progress they have made and of course, as you said, the hearing will increase the sincerity and…”

nodeData.topic: Day 02 · Preparing for the Battle of the Day
nodeData.note: SB 11.13.4; Siksastaka 2; BG 9.29; BG 4.11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Why the hour matters: time is one of the causes that shift the modes of nature, and both scripture and Ayurveda point to the last part of the night. The holy name is fully potent at every hour; what varies is our receptivity — Krishna reciprocates with our disposition to serve, and brahma-muhurta is when that receptivity is easiest. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Brahma-muhurta is the time when Krishna's internal energy is prominent; at other times the external energy and its modes prevail. At this hour we can be in tune with the internal energy. — “So we can be very much in tune with the internal energy”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:10 (auto-transcript): “That's the time today where the energy has its time. That's the time when the internal energy is very much prominent, whereas other times it's the external energy with the moods which is prevalent. So we can be very much in tune with the internal energy of doing that. In…”

In general, activities, mantras and purificatory rites are affected because the modes of nature become prominent differently at different times.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:45 (auto-transcript): “In general, the activities, mantras, and purificatory rituals, the modes of nature become differently prominent.”
The Bhagavatam lists ten factors that bring a mode forward — among them place and time.

The gunas are ever-changing influences, not fixed types of person; time decides which one becomes prominent, and in Krishna's list of ten causes place and time stand side by side.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:19 (auto-transcript): “The Gunas are ever-changing influences, not fixed personality types. The time affects which one becomes prominent. Side by side in Krishna's list of ten causes stand. Desha that is place and Kala that is time. One should do activities at Dramamurta, not at evening and…”

children.topic: Act at brahma-muhurta, not at night
children.note:
A further reference is read: spiritual activities should be done at brahma-muhurta, not in the evening or at midnight.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:37 (auto-transcript): “One should do activities at Dramamurta, not at evening and midnight. Srimad Bhagavan 11.3.6 Everyone walks into the mid-days, the liturgy.”

children.topic: Ayurveda: the day starts with rising
children.note:
Ayurveda's daily regimen (dinacarya) begins not with diet or exercise but with when to rise — the very window scripture recommends, though for a different purpose: protecting the lifespan.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:11 (auto-transcript): “It is a daily regimen. Dinner charia begins not with a diet or exercise but with when to rise. It identifies the very same window that Shastra recommends. Though for a different purpose, Rakshatam Ayushaha, protection of longevity. Different periods of the day are dominated…”

The last watch of the night is the vata period — light, mobile and clear, the bodily counterpart of the mental clarity scripture attributes to this hour. Near sunrise kapha takes over: heaviness and inertia return. That is why the acaryas speak of a muhurta, not just 'the morning'.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:52 (auto-transcript): “The last watch of the night is the Vata period, while the period being near sunrise is governed by Kapha. The last watch of the night is the Vata period, light, mobile and clear, the physiological counterpart to the mental clarity that Shastrak attributes to this hour. Near…”

children.topic: One more hour is a different world
children.note:
Sleeping an extra hour does not only make us later; it puts us in a different environment. — “Sleeping one more hour doesn't just make it later”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:42 (auto-transcript): “Sleeping one more hour doesn't just make it later, it places us in a different environment. The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine confirmed that this time keeping is not a vague brain level habit. It is a molecular mechanism running autonomously inside almost every…”

The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine showed that the body's timekeeping is a molecular mechanism running in almost every cell, keeping a near-24-hour rhythm on its own.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:50 (auto-transcript): “The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine confirmed that this time keeping is not a vague brain level habit. It is a molecular mechanism running autonomously inside almost every cell in the body. The clock is endogenous and self-sustaining. It holds a near 24 hour rhythm…”

As the day goes on the body wears down, mental anxiety and noise increase, and these influences seep into consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:46 (auto-transcript): “The body is not working on a normal person in the environment and in the modes gradually increase.”

children.topic: Heavier as the night goes on
children.note:
At events you can notice the mood getting heavier as the evening gets later.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:12 (auto-transcript): “For this reason, when you go to different events, you might notice that the moths get heavier and heavier as the evening gets later. The morning hours are important for any type of practice, especially prayers, meditation, chanting and reading. If we engage in any of these…”

So the morning hours are important for every kind of practice — prayer, meditation, chanting, reading — and what is done then carries more potential.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:22 (auto-transcript): “The morning hours are important for any type of practice, especially prayers, meditation, chanting and reading. If we engage in any of these activities in the morning, they will have more potential. I have invested all your potencies in those names and there are no hard and…”
Mahaprabhu's second verse: the Lord has put all his potencies in his names with no strict rules of time or place, yet he laments that, because of offences, he has no attachment for chanting.

children.topic: The treasure is there, but blocked
children.note:
A reflection is read: we may chant for years and still have material desires and bad habits — the treasure is available, but something keeps us from receiving it; this misfortune is called durdaiva.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:25 (auto-transcript): “is accessible but we cannot fully experience it. Reflections 1 verse 2. We may have chanted for a period of time and think I have been chanting for so many years and still I have material desires and bad habits. What is the point of all this chanting? Our treasure is…”

The potency of the name is always there; what we must watch is our own attentiveness. — “The potency is there, but we must also observe our level of attentiveness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 79:25 (auto-transcript): “The potency is there, but we must also observe our level of attentiveness. When it says that there are no hard and fast rules, it means that there is always benefit from the chanting, but some situations are more beneficial than others. It is not that we can only chant in the…”

'No hard and fast rules' means chanting always benefits, at any time, softly or loudly, in temple or home — but certain situations facilitate quality chanting and progress more than others.

🎙 Maharaj at 79:54 (auto-transcript): “There are no hard and fast rules, but certain situations facilitate quality chanting more than others. Right. It's facilitated about chanting, facilitated about progress more than other times. We are attention to love. The name is absolute, all potency, no rules of time.…”

children.topic: Nothing in past chanting is wasted
children.note:
The name is absolute and was never weaker at any hour, so none of our past chanting is demoted. If the name never varies, what varies? That is the question to explore. — “The name acted every single time.”

🎙 Maharaj at 80:25 (auto-transcript): “The name is absolute, all potency, no rules of time. Therefore, nothing was ever wrong with the name at any hour and nothing in your past chanting is demoted. The name acted every single time. Therefore, the words won't question. If the name never varies, what varies in mind?…”

Krishna's invitation is open to everyone: he is equal to all, yet he is especially with those who serve him. The equality is real and so is the asymmetry — the changing factor is on the devotee's side.
Krishna reciprocates in proportion to our surrender.

The exchange is personal because both Krishna and the devotee are conscious — not a signal picked up by a receiver, but a person responding to the direction of our heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 84:45 (auto-transcript): “The exchange is personal, not a broadcast met by a receiver, but a person who responds to the direction of our heart. What He reciprocates is not our schedule, our stamina, or our similarity. It is our response, our receptivity to His invitation expressed in service. How do…”

What Krishna reciprocates is not our schedule, stamina or similarity to others, but our response to his invitation, expressed in service. — “It is our response, our receptivity to His invitation expressed in service.”

🎙 Maharaj at 84:58 (auto-transcript): “What He reciprocates is not our schedule, our stamina, or our similarity. It is our response, our receptivity to His invitation expressed in service. How do we respond to what is available? When you say it, you get more. When you take it, you say it.”

A Padma Purana verse explains the mechanism: the material senses cannot grasp Krishna's name, form, qualities and pastimes; he reveals himself when the senses, beginning with the tongue, are engaged in his service.

The name is not captured by our senses; he appears to one who has the right disposition.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:53 (auto-transcript): “The name cannot be grasped by the material senses. We cannot make him appear. But when those same senses are engaged in service, beginning with the top, then he reveals himself. He appears to one with the right disposition. Variable is receptivity, same one, a disposition for…”

That disposition is for service — not a mood, a talent or a prior attainment — and it is available to anyone, at any stage, starting today.

🎙 Maharaj at 87:26 (auto-transcript): “Variable is receptivity, same one, a disposition for service, not a mood, not a talent, not a prior attainment, not an actress, not an actress. A disposition available to anyone at any stage beginning today. Why did every generation of our Gaudier Acharyas treasure the hours…”

Summing up: Mahaprabhu confesses he has no taste, Krishna reciprocates, the Padma Purana gives the mechanism — Krishna is always available, the practitioner is not always receptive. So the real question is not why the hour matters to the name, but when I am most receptive. — “but the Sadhaka is not always receptive.”

🎙 Maharaj at 90:13 (auto-transcript): “So far we saw Mahaprabhu's confession that I have no taste, Krishna's reciprocation, the Padma Purana's mechanism, and this gives us Krishna is always available, but the Sadhaka is not always receptive. The old question, why does the hour matter to the Holy Name? The real…”

children.topic: What is at stake in this hour?
children.note:
The name reveals himself wherever he finds a heart inclined to serve; the variable was never where you stand, but how you approach.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:05 (auto-transcript): “The name reveals himself wherever he finds a heart inclined to serve. The variable was never where you stand. It has always been how you approach it. In writing, if you wish, answer the following question for yourself.”

Participants are asked to write, for themselves only, an answer to: what is truly at stake in this hour? Nothing will be shared or graded.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:37 (auto-transcript): “In writing, if you wish, answer the following question for yourself.”

children.topic: Greeting the deity in the morning
children.note:
The deity is the representative of transcendence in this world. Coming in the morning to greet the deity and join the kirtan brings reciprocation; we are not always aware how the creeper of devotion is being watered, because the material energy is thick — but these activities do water it.

🎙 Maharaj at 105:10 (auto-transcript): “Ramamoharita Parmaipati. This is actually the representative of transcendence”

Questions and comments from participants; Maharaj's answers are mostly not captured.

🎙 Maharaj at 108:32 (auto-transcript): “the shape the Acharya part big that is not my question is it is said that we are about three and three and a half a.m. it is Brahmamurtha but if I work up early then three like one a.m. or two a.m. then will it work as a Brahmamurtha or it will not will work as a Brahmamurtha…”

If brahma-muhurta is around 3–3:30 a.m., is chanting after rising at 1 or 2 a.m. still brahma-muhurta, or tamas? Someone told the questioner to bathe only after 3 a.m.

🎙 Maharaj at 109:03 (auto-transcript): “and three and a half a.m. it is Brahmamurtha but if I work up early then three like one a.m. or two a.m. then will it work as a Brahmamurtha or it will not will work as a Brahmamurtha or it will work as a tamas like this it came from my experience that one day i wake up early…”

An Ayurvedic doctor in the US called the devotees' diet perfect, while one in India remarks that devotees have many health problems. Could improper meal times and missing brahma-muhurta be the reasons?

🎙 Maharaj at 112:01 (auto-transcript): “I met with an elevated doctor. She said that whatever diet you Hare Krishnas are following, actually it's a very perfect diet from an Ayurvedic perspective. And here in India, there is an Ayurvedic doctor who treats many devotees, including many sanyases as well. So one…”

Two devotees can do the same service with different consciousness. Can we purify our motive by our own effort, or does it come by itself one day? A participant had also noted that rising early is not enough without proper consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 118:25 (auto-transcript): “I have a question, like you said that there are same activities two devotees are doing, same activity, same day done, same java, same cooking, everything, but one devotee's consciousness behind that service is different, others is different. So Maharaj, can we correct our…”

nodeData.topic: Day 03 · Rising Early Tomorrow Comes by Preparing Tonight
nodeData.note: BG 14.6; BG 6.16 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma-muhurta is the hour of goodness, but goodness is only a means, not the goal; the hour helps us but cannot do our part. A good morning is decided the evening before — regulated eating, sleeping and winding down — and practised consistently rather than heroically, until the austerity becomes natural and the morning program is seen as a treasure. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Just as a place influences us — no one does peaceful japa in a brothel — time has a strong influence, because everything we do, even the demigods, is under the modes. Brahma-muhurta is the most favourable condition for prayer, chanting, hearing and meditation.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:11 (auto-transcript): “Just as a place influences us, yesterday we talked about it, they said, if you walk into a group of 100 hungry people, how do you feel? Comfortable? You can peacefully do japa there, if you enter a brothel, you do peaceful japa in the hotel, bliss the time has influence yes…”

The holy name is fully potent 24 hours a day; the limitation is never in the name. Our attentiveness and receptivity change with time and the modes. — “so the changing factor is us”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:34 (auto-transcript): “is always fully potent 24 hours they are not hard and fast rules regarding time the limitation is never in the name it is because everything about us is in the mood so the changing factor is us krishna's availability is constant but our attentiveness and receptivity according…”

It does not matter where we stand; what matters is consciousness. We can be close to someone thousands of kilometres away, and far from someone sitting beside us. — “What matters is your consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:15 (auto-transcript): “make advancement or rise above everything. Rising is not receptivity. Distance is not disqualification. For example, you said that the cow head balls, they want to touch Krishna? Yes. But it does not matter where you stand. What matters is your consciousness. You can touch…”

children.topic: What are we seeking in this hour?
children.note:
Before going further, Maharaj asks: what are we actually looking for at brahma-muhurta?

🎙 Maharaj at 25:03 (auto-transcript): “Before we go further, we should ask one important question. What is it that we are actually seeking in this hour? Is it important? Is it important? What are we looking for in this Brahmi Mohruta?”

For one who is suffering, time passes slowly; for one enjoying, it is short. — “Therefore time is relative, according to our consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:09 (auto-transcript): “or Father, according to a person who is suffering, the time is very slow. A person who is enjoying, the time is very short, very short. Therefore time is relative, according to our consciousness. Have we come all this way to become calm and do something? We have spent two…”

children.topic: Peace and clarity are not the goal
children.note:
Peace, clarity and a fresh, steady mind are valuable, but they are qualities of goodness, not the goal itself.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:17 (auto-transcript): “peace, clarity, a fresh, steady mind. Is that what we are looking for? To be peaceful. Sancti. Is that what we are looking for? These are all valuable, but they are, but are they the goal? They are the qualities of Satwa and Sri Krishna says.”

Cleanliness alone will not take us back to Godhead; outer cleanliness helps inner cleanliness so that Krishna can sit in the heart. In the same way the hour is a process, a means. — “external cleanliness should help us to have internal cleanliness”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:24 (auto-transcript): “Cleanliness. Cleanliness will take one back home back to God, eh? Cleanliness will take one back home back to God, eh? So, when we say cleanliness, what are we looking at? What are we looking at? Cleanliness. It's the greatest self for Krishna to enjoy, right? external…”
The mode of goodness is purer and illuminating, but it still conditions us through attachment to happiness and knowledge. — “goodness is still conditioning but we're using it”

children.topic: A better prison is still a prison
children.note:
Even a president or prime minister in a prison is a prisoner. We use goodness to advance, not to settle in it. — “a better prison is still a prison”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:38 (auto-transcript): “If you are a president, prime minister in a prison, what is it? You are in a prison. You are not free. whatever position we have as as a prisoner so a better prison is still a prison and this one has good light right does it make sense thank you to continue so the we've laid…”

children.topic: The hour won't do our part
children.note:
In brahma-muhurta the withdrawal of the senses (pratyahara) is largely done for us — no traffic, no phones, no voices, a lightness and clarity. But the hour asks less of us; it does not act in our place.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:54 (auto-transcript): “this part is what the yoga tradition calls Which means what? Kithara means rejecting or fermenting. The retraction of the senses from the object. We will draw the senses from the object and bring it in. We bring the senses inside, not leaving it outside. In the Brahma…”

children.topic: No one can eat for you
children.note:
Maharaj jokes: 'Don't go for prasadam, I'll eat for you; don't bathe, I'll bathe for you.' We must eat, bathe, read, chant and hear attentively ourselves. Distance has no effect, but receptivity does. — “we have to eat ourselves”

nodeData.topic: Day 04 · What Steals Away Our Brahma-muhurta From Us?
nodeData.note: CC Antya 20.16 (Siksastaka 2); BG 2.40 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Why don't we receive the treasure of the holy name at brahma-muhurta? Using Mahaprabhu's second Siksastaka verse and Bhaktivinoda Thakura's four anarthas — confusion about truth, thirst for the temporary, offences and weakness of heart — Maharaj diagnoses what steals our mornings, offers the acaryas' remedy, and names the modern thief: late-night screens and unspiritual association. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
The class opens with a skit Maharaj asks everyone to watch carefully: one devotee poses with the Bhagavad-gita for a selfie, eyes closed as if in samadhi, hunts for a caption, then drifts into talk about prices, traffic and other people's faults. Another meaning is shared: Acyuta never falls from his supreme position — and never lets go of our heart.

Everything in Krishna consciousness is devotional service, not a stage for our expertise; Krishna enjoys the love with which we serve, so focus matters.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:05 (auto-transcript): “consciously the whole environment be different that is kirtan so everything we do in christian consciousness is devotional service it is not the time for us to exercise our expertise christian do not enjoy our expertise in doing anything he enjoyed the look we have for him in…”
Mahaprabhu's second verse: though the Lord has made his names freely available, he laments that offences leave him without attachment to chanting.

Our beads 'fast', or japa drags from morning to night. The cause is no taste for the name because we have taste for temporary things — asat-trsna.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:26 (auto-transcript): “What is responsible for that? No taste. Please come to Asatrishna. Asatrishna means we have taste for temporary things, not taste for the Holy Name. That is the reason, the cause for that. We chant but we cannot fully experience the Holy Name even though everything is…”

It is like sitting at a feast of your favourite dishes while feeling ill: the food is there, but we cannot take it. The treasure is available; something blocks us. This is durdaiva, misfortune.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:00 (auto-transcript): “It's like being at a feast with your favorite preparation, but you feel sick and nourished. Although the food is available, we have not. Do we actually know where we struggle? A struggle that is not understood can only be endured; once understood, it can be addressed. — “Until a struggle is understood, it can only be endured.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:24 (auto-transcript): “Do we actually know where we struggle? Until a struggle is understood, it can only be endured. Once it is understood, it can be right. Commenting on this verse in Bhajana-rahasya, Bhaktivinoda Thakura names four anarthas behind durdaiva: tattva-vibhrama, asat-trsna, aparadha and hrdaya-daurbalya.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:08 (auto-transcript): “In Bhajan al-Hashya, commenting on these words, Srila Bhakti Bhattakura presents the answer. There are four things here, I mentioned it earlier, there are four things. One is Tatra, Vibrama, Asatrishna, Varadu, and Rudha, the valiant.”

We lack clear understanding of who we are, who Krishna is and our relationship. A pure devotee and we chant the same mantra with a different quality; knowledge must come first for faith to be strong. Many in the movement call themselves devotees yet in the heart do not accept Krishna as the Supreme Lord (BG 9.12 purport) — then service, chanting and relationships become mechanical.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:14 (auto-transcript): “Misconceptions about one's real identity and about Tatra. We don't have a complete understanding or clear understanding about who we are, who is Krishna, the Supreme, but it's our relationship with him. Let's try to understand this because even a small child in Krishna…”

children.topic: Why the Gosvamis gave up everything
children.note:
Knowing that we are eternally Krishna's servants is what let the six Gosvamis leave very high positions to live in Vrindavan; renunciation is easy for a poor man, not for a minister.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:10 (auto-transcript): “Can you imagine the Sikh Goswami giving up the high position, material position, very high position, to come and wear a cow pin in Brindavan? What is making them to do? like that. What is that? They have an understanding about who they are and the position of Krishna.…”

Desires for material objects, heaven, mystic power and impersonal liberation. It is subtle and lies deep in the heart. Every time the temporary becomes more attractive than Krishna's invitation at dawn, we are seeing asat-trsna.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:26 (auto-transcript): “Hunkering for that quote is temporary. Asat Trishna. Asat Trishna. Now, Asatrishna means he has divisions. He has divisions also. One, Asatrishna. Asatrishna has many qualities. Many qualities. Name them. Try. Try. Give some. Just saying a question is general. Desire for…”

Ten offences to the name, offences in the holy dhama (even playing with one's feet in the Ganga on parikrama), offences in seva, against other living entities and against Vaishnavas — envy, not offering respect, anger. Maharaj contrasts Jatila, who serves Krishna's pleasure, with the fault-finder Ramacandra Puri, and plays on the word: apa-radha, 'no Radha' — no Radha, no Krishna. Offences do not lessen Krishna's mercy; they lessen our capacity to receive it.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:34 (auto-transcript): “How many of them? No, not only three. Apparat, not only three. How many? One? Nam Apparat, very good. Nam Apparat, how many? Ten. See, just one alone. You got ten. Nam Apparat is ten. Very good. Nam Apparat, because we're going to let go for that. Ten. So, so ten. Offenses…”

Weakness of heart binds us to the world: attachment to things unrelated to Krishna, hypocrisy, envy and the desire for prestige; an inability to let go of attachments, insecurities and ego. Why should a devotee be insecure, when Krishna has clearly declared the devotee's destination (BG 4.9)?

One sign of weakness of heart is envy of others' prosperity and recognition.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:06 (auto-transcript): “objects unrelated to Krishna, hypocrisy, envy, Kupi Nyapi, her envy of the prosperity of others, her desire for prestige and position. When Rupa Gosvami read the introduction of his Vidagdha-madhava, Mahaprabhu praised him while watching the other devotees' faces, to see how they felt — teaching us how to behave.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:24 (auto-transcript): “That time Rupa Goswami was writing his book, Viddagda Madhaba, and the introduction, very, very nice, very sweet. A purport of Srila Prabhupada is read: a Vaishnava rejoices when another is empowered to spread the holy name; one envious of that is not a Vaishnava, and such envy is to be neglected. Maharaj notes Prabhupada was speaking of the envy shown toward himself.

Learning, even of Sanskrit, does not take one back to Godhead; one must become a pure devotee free from envy of other devotees — that is the proof of Krishna consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:37 (auto-transcript): “There is no Sanskrit. Come, I will teach you Sanskrit. Sanskrit is the goal of going back to Godhead. That is the goal of the Christian concept. Sanskrit. So, if you are not Sanskrit, you are purely Godhead. Prakasananda Saraswati, you went back to Godhead. Do you know…”

Krishna promises there is no loss on this path and even a little advancement protects from the greatest fear. What comes to mind on hearing this? Hope — and Krishna is not a bluffer; he has what he promises. The anarthas obstruct but cannot erase our devotion; still, avoid them.

children.topic: Why the acaryas analyse our struggle
children.note:
Out of compassion, like parents who know a child's illness and medicine. Bhaktivinoda Thakura is happy to see someone chant — not for his own gain, but because he loves Krishna, and therefore loves us.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:30 (auto-transcript): “detrimental for our practice. Thinking corner. This is? Thinking corner. Thinking, let us ask a question. Devotees interfere where Krishna does not. Gadadhara Dasa boldly went to a hostile Kazi: Mahaprabhu and Nityananda have delivered everyone, only you are left — chant Krishna today. When the Kazi said 'tomorrow I'll chant Hari', Gadadhara replied that he had already said the name. Preach boldly, not offensively.

🎙 Maharaj at 79:15 (auto-transcript): “In Chichanga Bhagwat, he said, devotee of Nita Nambu, Gadadaradas, Gadadaradas. These struggles are common to every sincere practitioner; the right diagnosis gives the right remedy. A gardener must tell the plant he sowed from the weeds that spring up with it. Those doing wonderfully today also struggled; sincere, praying effort is answered.

🎙 Maharaj at 82:39 (auto-transcript): “For a gardener, a gardener have this experience. every garden has this experience that the plant you planted will not be the only thing that will come out from there. children.topic: Cultivate what nourishes, avoid what weakens
children.note: The acaryas give not just a diagnosis but medicine. Rupa Gosvami distilled it into Upadesamrta verses 2 and 3: six things that destroy bhakti and six that nourish it.

Compassion means being unable to bear others' suffering and doing whatever it takes to help. The acaryas wrote and printed books so we have the medicine today. Not to read them is ingratitude — drinking poison knowingly, like refusing the rope thrown to us in a well.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:16 (auto-transcript): “Writing and printing. How much is important? What are they given to printing? Distribute books, distribute books, distribute books, print books, print books, distribute, print books, distribute books. Is it for making money? No. For scholarship? No. For benefit. Because they…”

children.topic: Greedy for service, patient for mercy
children.note:
How can one be both greedy and patient? A devotee answers: greedy for service, patient for mercy. Endeavour and attitude are friends — we serve with all our strength, present our case, and let Krishna respond when he sees fit; we do not make him our houseboy. — “Greedy for the service but patient for the mercy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 95:44 (auto-transcript): “How is that? How is that? that you want to be spiritually greedy and patient. How a greedy person can be patient? A greedy person can be patient. If you are patient, then you are not greedy. And if you are greedy, you cannot be patient. Is it not true? Is it true or not? I'm…”

Live today as if it is the last day: no procrastination, no thinking we have 80 years left — especially in Kali-yuga, where nothing is certain — and leave the results to Krishna.

nodeData.topic: Day 04 (second upload) · What Steals Away Our Brahma-muhurta From Us?
nodeData.note: CC Antya 20.16 (Siksastaka 2); BG 2.40 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Why don't we receive the treasure of the holy name at brahma-muhurta? Using Mahaprabhu's second Siksastaka verse and Bhaktivinoda Thakura's four anarthas — confusion about truth, thirst for the temporary, offences and weakness of heart — Maharaj diagnoses what steals our mornings, offers the acaryas' remedy, and names the modern thief: late-night screens and unspiritual association. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Opening skit: two kinds of association
children.note:
The class opens with a skit Maharaj asks everyone to watch carefully: one devotee poses with the Bhagavad-gita for a selfie, eyes closed as if in samadhi, hunts for a caption, then drifts into talk about prices, traffic and other people's faults. nodeData.topic: Day 05 · How to Make Rising Early a Lifelong Habit
nodeData.note: BG 9.14 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The closing VIHE class gathers the week into a personal blueprint: plan the evening so that the morning simply carries out a decision already made. Maharaj teaches mindful reading, consistency in small daily acts like the Vrindavan widow's pot of water, Brahma-muhurta as a daily return to our identity as Krishna's servant, attentive hearing of the holy name, prayer and gratitude, and keeping the practice alive together with other devotees.
